study type: Diagnostic accuracy study (secondary analysis of existing data)
cohort: The study assessed 21 EWS in 2560 women from 46 countries with suspected or confirmed infections during pregnancy and the post-pregnancy period.
finding: No single early warning system demonstrated sufficient diagnostic accuracy to be used alone to identify sepsis, but obstetric- and sepsis-specific EWS performed better for early identification of maternal sepsis than non-obstetric and non-sepsis-specific scoring systems.
